items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew John Neves, the Neves Brothers.

ctx.x: You were talking about meeting other younger musicians around Boston, and Boston was a fairly interesting scene, in part because there were some academic institutions there... I’m wondering who some of the people were who you formed early affiliations with.

After working with the Four Sounds, my next memorable gig was with a trumpet player named Phil Barboza. He was a trumpet player, and he had a Latin group. It was timbales, bass, trumpet, and piano—and conga. I didn’t know anything about Latin music. I forget how I got the gig actually. Maybe through the timbale player. But I became real good friends with Bill Fitch, who was the conga player in the band. Bill was a Boston guy, and he was deep into Afro-Cuban music. He saw that I didn’t know how to play Latin…
So you moved to New York in ‘59?
